subject: Private deployment provenance: snapshot stewardship options and operator certification
content:
From: Lenora Williams <lenora.williams@healthsync.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
Cc: HealthSync Procurement <ctown_procurement@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, May 2, 2028 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Deployment provenance and evidence for on-prem instance (questions)

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we work through the MSA + Order Form for the on-prem deployment, our legal and security teams have surfaced a few specific asks around deployment provenance, operator access, and a lightweight escrow-like pathway for snapshots. High level: we need to be comfortable that (a) the snapshot delivered for witness/testing is verifiable and timebound, (b) operator access is auditable and limited, and (c) there's a clear proof-of-possession / deletion pathway in the event of termination.

Questions:
- Do you support signed snapshot manifests (hash + timestamp + signer) for delivered snapshots?
- Can an independent witness (our security vendor) observe or verify a snapshot delivery? If so, what is the suggested process and what access would you require?
- For operator access during on-prem installs, can you agree to an operator certification process and a short-lived temporary console account model (e.g., timeboxed access that requires an access request + approval flow)?
- Are there options for an escrow-like handoff (sealed copy with a neutral custodian) if we need to retain a copy for regulatory continuity?

We're not asking to create a heavy on-prem escrow, but we need contractual language and an operational proposal we can present to our auditors. Happy to hop on a call, but asking for an initial proposal we can share internally first.

Thanks,
Lenora
Lenora Williams
Head of Security & Compliance
HealthSync

---
From: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
To: Lenora Williams <lenora.williams@healthsync.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, May 2, 2028 at 11:04 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance and evidence for on-prem instance (questions)

Lenora —

Appreciate the clear list. I've looped in Alex (ops + evidence playbooks), Jordan (legal ops lead), and Karthik (custody/escrow options) so we can give a consolidated response and a lightweight operational proposal. High-level answers up front and then a proposed path:

High-level: yes to signed manifests and witness verification; operator access can be timeboxed and auditable; escrow-like custody is possible as an optional add-on (sealed snapshot with neutral custodian) but we prefer a staged evidence handoff for routine cases.

Proposed pathway (summary):
1) Snapshot manifests: delivered snapshots include a manifest.json with SHA-256 hashes for the snapshot artifact, generation timestamp (UTC), and a Redwood signing certificate fingerprint. We can deliver both the snapshot and a detached signature for third-party verification.
2) Witness verification: we can host a short remote witness session (shared screen + checksum handshake) or permit an on-site witness to observe a snapshot export. For higher assurance, we can deliver to a neutral S3 bucket with pre-signed URL and provide the detached signature and manifest for the witness to verify.
3) Operator certification & timeboxed access: we propose a formal operator certification attestation (operator identity + training record) and a temporary access model: console keys issued for a bounded window (e.g., 6 hours) with mandatory session recording and audit log export.
4) Escrow-like custody: two options — (A) sealed snapshot deposit with a neutral custodian (Redwood coordinates; custodian provides chain-of-custody receipt) or (B) staged evidence handoff where Redwoods holds the signed manifest and proof artifacts and provides secure transfer on termination. Option A has more cost and legal overhead; Option B is our default.

I've attached a short runbook draft (snapshot_stewardship_runbook.pdf) that sketches the operational bits above and a doc with suggested MSA annex language. Alex/Jordan/Karthik — please add specifics / redline suggestions in replies.

Next step: Lenora, if this looks reasonable we can schedule a 30-minute sync with your security and procurement teams next week and draft a targeted annex to the MSA + Order Form.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments (2): snapshot_stewardship_runbook.pdf (12 KB) — short operational playbook; proposed-msa-annex-redlines.docx (48 KB) — language draft

---
From: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com
To: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, Lenora Williams <lenora.williams@healthsync.com>
Date: Thu, May 3, 2028 at 10:18 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance and evidence for on-prem instance (questions)

Thanks Mina — quick technical/legal comments and redline suggestions below (summary first, details inline):

Summary suggestions for annex:
- Snapshot manifest: require SHA-256 + RFC3339 timestamp + Redwood signer DN; add clause that manifest and detached signature will be retained for 12 months post-termination for audit (unless customer requests deletion earlier).
- Witnessing: allow either remote or on-site witness; if on-site, require mutually agreed 2-week window and Redwood personnel list; if remote, require encrypted transfer and ephemeral URL.
- Operator access: define "Operator" persona and require customer approval for named operators; restrict access to console and ephemeral keys only; require session recording kept for 90 days.
- Escrow pathway: prefer "Staged Evidence Handoff" as default (lower friction). If custodian escrow chosen, require custodian acceptance of standard chain-of-custody SLA and cost pass-through.

Inline redlines (highlights):
- Section X.2 (Snapshot Delivery): add a bullet requiring the manifest signature to be verifiable via Redwood's public certificate (we will publish a certificate fingerprint in the MSA exhibit).
- Section X.3 (Witnessing): add language clarifying that witness verification is limited to checksum verification and not access to customer data beyond the snapshot itself.
- Section X.4 (Operator Access): add requirement that any operator session that modifies production configurations must be approved in writing and trigger a 24-hour rollback window test.

I attached the proposed-msa-annex-redlines.docx with tracked changes. Jordan, can your team confirm whether the 12-month retention for manifest/signatures is acceptable? Karthik, please confirm custody vendor requirements and whether we should include a vendor whitelist placeholder.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-msa-annex-redlines.docx

---
From: mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
To: Lenora Williams <lenora.williams@healthsync.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com, jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, May 5, 2028 at 03:28 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment provenance and evidence for on-prem instance (questions)

Lenora —

Thanks for the quick read-through. Sounds like we're aligned on the proposed pathway. Next steps I suggest:
1) HealthSync procurement/legal: review the two attachments and flag any redlines you need (I know Jordan will coordinate on the MSA annex language).
2) If you want a witness run: pick remote vs on-site. For remote, we can schedule a short session next week and provide pre-signed download links + detached signature for verification.
3) If you prefer a sealed custodian escrow, note that will require a brief statement of work and custodian acceptance; we can provide vendor contacts and a cost estimate.

I am happy to join a 30-minute call next Tue/Wed; otherwise Jordan will follow up on the specific MSA language and retention durations.

DocuSign: once legal confirms redlines, we can route the annex and order form via DocuSign (link prepared: https://app.docusign.com/link/ABC123).

Appreciate the collaboration — we want this to be as light as possible operationally while giving your auditors clear artifacts.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
